central_topic: Predicting full-benchmark binary accuracy and model rankings from a small shared item subset using historical source-model responses, score-directed acquisition, and source-trained score decoding.
core_methods: Source-weighted conditional full-score covariance acquisition with a fixed, nested, content-group-unique item path
All-query full-score ridge regression with an optional difficulty-centered offset blend
Optional prefix-only penalized log-odds shift, full-population score curve, and residual ridge decoder
Earlier frozen-surrogate pilot plus randomized audit residual correction, including unequal-content-group weighting
Source-lineage-held-out selection and decoder tuning with nested refitting for the nonlinear candidate
comparators: Uniform item subsampling and source-prior prediction
Response-vector clustering and weighted anchor estimates, as in Anchor Points
Item response theory and compact benchmark estimation, as in tinyBenchmarks
Supervised reference-instance prediction, as in 100 instances is all you need
Adaptive item acquisition, as in Active Evaluation Acquisition; conceptual rather than experimentally evaluated here
Model-assisted finite-population estimation and generalized difference estimators
benchmarks: Final evaluation: bbh, gpqa, mmlu_pro, musr, openllm_math, legalbench, math, med_qa, mmlu
Open LLM Leaderboard and HELM binary matrices in benchmark-prediction snapshot 55faff496947789f94e6b5908c77cbc3e84f81ad
architectural_shifts: Estimator architecture: frozen item-response reconstruction plus random-audit correction versus direct all-observation score ridge; acquisition also changes between these packages
Implemented optional extension from linear score decoding to a scalar log-odds curve plus prefix-matched residual ridge, with score-directed acquisition unchanged
No neural architecture transition or architecture-specific transfer result is established; groups are anonymous and nonlinear decoder activation is unverified
result_driven_themes: Score-directed acquisition and all-query decoding deserve primary positioning: development MAE 0.055403088322603176 versus frozen-audit MAE 0.0810613202961334; individual mechanisms are not isolated

The optional nonlinear candidate has development MAE 0.05464601737059244 versus its linear predecessor's 0.055403088322603176; no between-variant interval or ablation establishes the cause or significance of this small difference
Final nine-case evaluation gives candidate MAE 0.038991605535293065 versus recorded IRT 0.05911223215296765 and uniform 0.10520541810011626
Paired lineage-block bootstrap intervals favor the final candidate over recorded baselines conditional on fixed cases, not on complete ancestry separation or universal generalization
Ranking remains a co-objective: final Spearman 0.8158480130897703 and Kendall 0.6715966634525837; design-unbiased score estimation does not guarantee ranking accuracy
Development and final evaluations use different benchmark sets and seeds; absolute metrics must not be presented as a paired improvement

queries.query: c-optimal experimental design regularized regression linear functional prediction
queries.rationale: The strongest packages use squared conditional covariance with full score divided by regularized item variance and decode all responses with ridge. Seek foundational prediction-directed design theory, without asserting exact c-optimal equivalence or an isolated selector gain.

queries.query: Rasch model fixed item difficulty penalized ability estimation
queries.rationale: The optional decoder uses logits of source item means as fixed difficulty-like offsets, fits a penalized scalar shift from each queried prefix, and adds residual ridge. Rasch/logistic latent-trait work supplies conceptual positioning, not evidence of full IRT fitting or verified nonlinear activation.

queries.query: model assisted survey sampling generalized difference estimator residual correction
queries.rationale: The earlier evaluated variant freezes pilot-only predictions and estimates residual totals through random audits with unequal-group correction. Generalized difference estimation grounds its conditional unshrunk, unclipped score-unbiasedness argument, not empirical superiority or unbiased rankings.

queries.query: "Anchor Points: Benchmarking Models with Much Fewer Examples"
queries.rationale: Weighted clustering anchors are expected related work and a recorded baseline family. Resolve supplied arXiv:2309.08638 directly; do not assume the local baseline exactly reproduces the published method.

IRT is the strongest recorded final baseline, making compact IRT-based estimation essential context. Resolve supplied arXiv:2402.14992 and distinguish its full method from the local IRT implementation.

queries.query: "100 instances is all you need" "predicting the success of a new LLM"
queries.rationale: The supplied arXiv:2409.03563 is the nearest supervised reference-instance prediction literature. Compare its target and protocol with direct score ridge and prefix-matched residual regression; no experimental reproduction is established.

queries.query: "Active Evaluation Acquisition for Efficient LLM Benchmarking"
queries.rationale: Resolve supplied arXiv:2410.05952 to distinguish adaptive acquisition from the run's source-only fixed shared path. This is conceptual coverage: per-target adaptation is unsupported by the interface and was not evaluated.

queries.rationale: Resolve supplied arXiv:2406.01574 for a final benchmark and leaderboard component. The final set also contains mmlu, but no MMLU-to-MMLU-Pro transfer mechanism is established.
